# Money Should Never Be Why a Child Stops Playing

## Stance

Whatever the club charges, no child should leave Fernhollow because their family cannot pay. If that happens, it is a failure of how we set fees, not of the family.

## Scope

Junior members. Adults are different: they choose to pay for themselves, though I would still not turn an adult away over money. It does not mean fees should be low for everyone; families who can pay should.

## Why I Think This

Fifteen years of community nursing taught me how little it takes to tip a household over, and how rarely people ask for help until it is late. A £25 rise is small on a spreadsheet and not small in January. I voted with the majority in spirit on 10 March (as chair I did not vote), because the club needed the income, but I agreed with [[ravinder-sahota]] about who would feel it ([[board-meeting-2026-03-10]]).

## What Would Change My Mind

Not the stance. The method is open: if the bursary reaches the families who need it without them feeling ashamed to ask, a flat fee is fine; if it does not, Ravinder's sliding scale is better ([[should-fees-use-a-sliding-scale]]).

## Implications

- The bursary is mentioned in every fee communication, first paragraph.
- Coaches are told how to point families to help without judging.
- The January 2027 review should ask whether any family left for cost reasons we could have prevented ([[did-the-fee-rise-cost-us-members]]).
